ProDHCPServer 1.2.0 fits small laptop screens and can update itself. Everything the app does on the network is unchanged from 1.1.0.

## What's new

- **Fits small laptop screens.** On a 1366x768 laptop, or a bigger screen with Windows scaling at 125% or 150%, the window now switches by itself to a compact layout: smaller text, shorter buttons and tighter spacing, so the status checks and device panel have room. Make the window bigger and it switches back. This works in every look and in Settings. The window also fits a 1366x768 screen at 125% scaling now, which it didn't before.
- **Size setting.** Under Settings (the gear button, or Ctrl+,), below **Dark or light**: **Automatic** (the default) picks the size from the window, **Large** always uses the big layout, **Compact** always uses the small one.
- **Updates from inside the app.** When the laptop has internet, ProDHCPServer checks GitHub for a newer release a few seconds after it starts. If there is one, a green banner offers **Install and restart**. It downloads the new version, checks it against the published SHA-256, swaps it in and restarts. Stop the server first. If any step fails, nothing is changed. On an isolated AV network the check just doesn't happen. You can turn it off, or check by hand, under Settings > Updates.

> [!NOTE]
> 1.1.0 and older can't update themselves, so download 1.2.0 by hand this one time. From 1.2.0 on, the app tells you when the next version is out.

## Download

1. Download `ProDHCPServer-v1.2.0-win-x64.exe` below. It's a single file: nothing to install, no .NET runtime needed. Replace your old copy with it; your profiles and settings carry over.
2. Double-click it. Windows asks for administrator rights, because changing adapter settings and serving DHCP need them.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **The exe isn't code-signed yet.** The first time you run it, Windows SmartScreen says "Windows protected your PC": click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. On IT-managed work laptops, Microsoft Defender's attack surface reduction rules may block it outright. Run it on an unmanaged laptop, or ask IT to allow a fixed folder (for example `C:\Tools\ProDHCPServer\`).

To check the download wasn't corrupted, compare its SHA-256 with the `.sha256` file below. In PowerShell: `Get-FileHash .\ProDHCPServer-v1.2.0-win-x64.exe`

## Everything else

The DHCP server, status checks, ping graphs, profiles with manufacturer presets, log export, device discovery and the looks are as in [1.1.0](https://github.com/cookingwithsimon/ProDHCPServer/releases/tag/v1.1.0) and [1.0.0](https://github.com/cookingwithsimon/ProDHCPServer/releases/tag/v1.0.0), which also lists the known limits.

Found a problem on site? [Open an issue](https://github.com/cookingwithsimon/ProDHCPServer/issues/new/choose) with the **Problem on site** form and include the session log.
